title: BART service invoices checked against work at stations
question: What did inspectors observe on site, what did vendors bill, and what did BART recover?
finding: BART recovered $11,900 on power washing and pursued $16,713 for sweeping. The FY2025 annual report gives $28,613 in settlements with two contractors for unperformed services. BART later confirmed a separate $57,655 recovery for medical crews.
how: Each row traces a separate published contractor investigation to the fiscal-year report addressing the response. The dollar finding is the original improper billing figure. The recovery column requires explicit confirmation by the inspector general.
limits: The two FY2025 amounts add to the reported settlement total. Adding that total to the two amounts would double-count them. The sweeping finding is a minimum and its individual receipt remains unverified. Some contract activity was outside San Francisco. The three investigative samples do not estimate error rates across all contracts.

rows.test: September 2023 records and observations identified 22 cleanings outside agreed standards. BART sometimes requested unscheduled work, without documenting changes as required.
rows.outcome: The FY2025 midyear report confirmed recovery of $11,900. General Counsel settled for that sum and declined further penalties.

rows.service: Overnight sweeping of station plazas and parking areas
rows.test: Inspectors identified at least $5,500 for 35 cleanings using observations, invoices and work reports. The contractor cited parked vehicles. The contract also required manual cleaning where machines could not reach.
rows.outcome: At midyear BART pursued $16,713 for sweeping. The FY2025 annual report gives $28,613 in settlements with two service contractors, matching $11,900 plus $16,713. The report does not itemize a sweeping cash receipt.

rows.service: Emergency medical crews at downtown San Francisco stations
rows.test: Investigators compared video, staffing, payroll and licenses. Three individuals lacked the required EMT license across 189 shifts and on seven occasions one EMT worked alone when two were billed.
rows.outcome: The FY2026 semiannual report confirmed recovery of $57,655. Basic life support training held by the three workers did not satisfy the contractual licensure requirement.

sources.t: FY2025 annual report, financial results, printed p. 2 (PDF)
